title: ZFS lab: a RAIDZ pool, datasets, snapshots, a failed disk and a scrub
summary: One server with four empty 2 GiB disks beside its system disk, there to be pooled and wiped. ZFS is volume manager and file system in one: the exercises build a RAIDZ pool, carve datasets with compression, take snapshots and roll back, take a disk offline and watch the pool resilver, scrub it, copy a dataset with send and receive, and rebuild the pool as two mirrors to compare the space. The ZFS half of qlab's raid-lab, extended.

exercises.title: ZFS anatomy
exercises.text: ZFS replaces the partition, the volume manager and the file system with one stack: a pool of disks (vdevs), datasets mounted from it, checksums on every block. The module and the tools come with Ubuntu; the four lab disks are empty.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the four lab disks, never the system one
lsmod | grep '^zfs'; zfs version
sudo zpool list    # no pools available yet

exercises.title: A RAIDZ pool
exercises.text: zpool create takes whole disks and a layout. raidz (RAIDZ1) stripes data with one disk of parity across the four: any one disk may fail. The pool is mounted at /tank at once.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the four lab disks, never the system one
sudo zpool create -f tank raidz $DISKS
sudo zpool status tank    # raidz1-0 over the four disks, ONLINE
sudo zpool list -o name,size,alloc,free,health tank
df -h /tank

exercises.title: Datasets and compression
exercises.text: A dataset is a file system cut from the pool with its own properties, and it takes only what it uses. compression=lz4 is free in practice: this text compresses several times over.

commands: sudo zfs create tank/data && sudo zfs set compression=lz4 tank/data
yes 'the same line, again and again, compresses very well' | head -c 50M | sudo tee /tank/data/text.bin >/dev/null
sudo zfs get -H -o value compressratio tank/data    # well above 1.00x
sudo zfs list -o name,used,avail,refer,mountpoint

exercises.title: Snapshots and rollback
exercises.text: A snapshot is a read-only view of a dataset at an instant, free until the data diverges. zfs diff shows what changed since; rollback puts the dataset back as it was.

commands: echo version-1 | sudo tee /tank/data/file
sudo zfs snapshot tank/data@v1
echo version-2 | sudo tee /tank/data/file
sudo zfs list -t snapshot; sudo zfs diff tank/data@v1
sudo zfs rollback tank/data@v1 && cat /tank/data/file    # version-1 again

exercises.title: A failed disk, a resilver, a scrub
exercises.text: Take one disk offline and the pool keeps serving, DEGRADED; bring it back and ZFS resilvers only the blocks it missed. A scrub reads every block against its checksum: the cheap insurance a cron job should run.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the four lab disks, never the system one
sudo zpool offline tank $(echo $DISKS | cut -d' ' -f1) && sudo zpool status tank    # DEGRADED, still serving
echo written-while-degraded | sudo tee /tank/data/degraded
sudo zpool online tank $(echo $DISKS | cut -d' ' -f1) && sleep 2 && sudo zpool status tank    # resilvered
sudo zpool scrub tank && sleep 3 && sudo zpool status tank    # scrub repaired 0B, No known data errors

exercises.title: send and receive
exercises.text: zfs send turns a snapshot into a stream, zfs receive makes a dataset out of it: a backup, a copy to another pool or another machine over SSH, incremental with -i.

commands: sudo zfs snapshot tank/data@backup
sudo zfs send tank/data@backup | sudo zfs receive tank/copy
sudo zfs list; cat /tank/copy/file
sudo zfs destroy -r tank/copy

exercises.title: Mirrors instead of RAIDZ, then tear it all down
exercises.text: Two mirrored pairs striped together: half the space of the four disks, but any disk of each pair may fail and resilvers copy a whole disk at full speed. Compare AVAIL with the RAIDZ pool, then leave the disks empty.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the four lab disks, never the system one
sudo zpool destroy tank
sudo zpool create -f tank mirror $(echo $DISKS | cut -d' ' -f1,2) mirror $(echo $DISKS | cut -d' ' -f3,4)
sudo zpool status tank; sudo zfs list tank    # mirror-0 and mirror-1; less AVAIL than raidz
sudo zpool destroy tank
for d in $DISKS; do sudo zpool labelclear -f $d; sudo wipefs -a $d; done
lsblk    # four empty disks again
